lessonPuzzle.backgroundText: Bathrooms are places where we keep things clean. Washing hands with soap helps chase away germs that you can’t see. Soap grabs the yucky stuff and water whooshes it away!
lessonPuzzle.question: When should you wash your hands?

answers.text: Only if your hands are wearing gloves

lessonPuzzle.successResponse: Yes! Super clean choice! 🧼✨ Next clue unlocked!
lessonPuzzle.failureResponse: Almost! Think about staying healthy—try again, champion! 🌟

clueToNextTag.text: Now it’s time to go on a BIG adventure… down, down, down to the basement! Find the rec-room where fun happens. Look for a mirror that shows your awesome face. The next tag is waiting near that mirror—like a secret reflection friend!
clueToNextTag.hint1: Go downstairs to the basement (down the stairs).
clueToNextTag.hint2: Find the rec-room—the fun room for games or hanging out.
clueToNextTag.hint3: Look near the mirror in the basement rec-room.

UIInfo.title: Clean Hands, Clever Mind
UIInfo.subtitle: You’ve unlocked another step—keep it moving.

lessonPuzzle.backgroundText: Soap helps remove germs because it breaks down oils and grime that germs stick to. Scrubbing for about 20 seconds gives the soap time to work and helps rinse everything away.
lessonPuzzle.question: About how long should you scrub with soap when washing your hands?
lessonPuzzle.successResponse: Correct. Smooth and smart. ✅ Next clue is yours.
lessonPuzzle.failureResponse: Not quite—think of the 'happy birthday' trick. Try again.

clueToNextTag.text: Next scan is in the basement. Head to the rec-room (the hangout/game area). You’re looking for a mirror—something reflective where you can see yourself. The next tag is staged near that mirror.
clueToNextTag.hint3: Near the mirror in the basement rec-room.

lessonPuzzle.backgroundText: Handwashing is a prevention system: soap acts as a surfactant that helps lift oils and particles from skin. Friction plus time improves removal, and running water carries contaminants away.
lessonPuzzle.question: Which combination is most important for effective handwashing?
lessonPuzzle.successResponse: Correct. Prevention wins. 🧠✅ Next clue unlocked.
lessonPuzzle.failureResponse: Not it. Think: soap needs friction and time to do its job.

clueToNextTag.text: Next location: basement rec-room. Find the mirror—any reflective surface meant for checking your appearance. The next tag is placed near that mirror, in plain reach, not buried.
clueToNextTag.hint2: Look for something reflective: mirror, framed glass, or a wall-mounted mirror.
clueToNextTag.hint3: Near the mirror in the basement rec-room.

lessonPuzzle.backgroundText: Handwashing reduces transmission pathways by mechanically removing contaminants. Soap disrupts oils, friction increases removal, and sufficient duration improves effectiveness before rinse carry-off.
lessonPuzzle.question: What best explains why soap-and-scrub handwashing works?

answers.text: Soap loosens oils; friction lifts debris; time improves removal
Soap sterilizes skin instantly on contact
Warm water alone kills all pathogens
Dry towels remove germs without washing

lessonPuzzle.successResponse: Correct. Proceed to the next node. ✅
lessonPuzzle.failureResponse: Incorrect. The mechanism is removal and disruption, not instant sterilization. Try again.

clueToNextTag.text: Proceed to the basement rec-room. Locate the mirror. Next tag is staged adjacent to the mirror on a reachable surface (not inside drawers or cabinets).
clueToNextTag.hint1: Downstairs to the basement, then into the rec-room.
clueToNextTag.hint2: Mirror is your landmark—reflective, intended for viewing.
clueToNextTag.hint3: Near the mirror in the basement rec-room.
